plan.title: [framework-gap] BLOCKER Planning-only documentation commit is denied by prospective scope-cover despite supported Path A publication

narratives.Description: A consumer that stages only planning files (design and decision Markdown, proposed or pending briefs, decision records, CHANGELOG.md and a shape-checked ordered-plan file) is denied at `git commit` by prospective scope-cover (#5656), because the gate asks for a ready running scope whose file_scope covers every non-xbrief path. This story adds a whole-set planning-publication classifier that runs on the raw staged index entries before the ready-scope guard and admits only that closed set. Any other staged set, and every classifier refuse, falls through to today's rules unchanged.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator publishing approved planning work while an unrelated implementation scope is active or not ready, I want a commit that holds only design documents, decisions, proposed or pending briefs, CHANGELOG.md and the ordered-plan file to pass the commit hook, so that I can publish the planning PR without activating an implementation scope or editing the active plan.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/hooks/planning-publication.ts: `listStagedIndexEntries` (git diff --cached --raw -z --no-abbrev --no-renames --diff-filter=ACMRDT; each NUL-delimited path handed on unmodified, with change kind, new mode and new blob id) and `classifyPlanningPublicationSet` (inventory: changelog entry path and `.deft/plan-sequence.json` from the #5477 set plus `docs/design/<name>.md` and `docs/decisions/<name>.md`; neutral: `<name>.xbrief.json` or `<name>.vbrief.json` one segment deep under a #5477 lifecycle folder other than active/, and `<name>.decision.json` under xbrief/decisions/ or vbrief/decisions/; each entry mode 100644 of kind A or M, or kind D; a non-deleted plan-sequence index blob must pass `isClosedPlanSequenceShape`, which already admits `insert_approvals` rows from #6205).
2. packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts: the Shell git commit decision reads staged entries through the widened seam (`listStagedIndexEntries`, `readStagedBlob`); `evaluateProspectiveScopeCover` takes optional `stagedEntries`, runs the classifier on them before path normalization, and returns the admission after the lifecycle-only return and before the story binding and ready-scope guard. A refuse is never a deny; it falls through. `isLifecycleOrInstallerRelPath` is unchanged.
3. Tests: classifier and producer unit tests (planning-publication.test.ts) and hook-decision regressions (dispatcher-planning-publication.test.ts) for every case in the P4 limb, including real-index cases (symlink, executable, typechange, stage-then-edit, malformed plan-sequence, leading-space and trailing-CR paths) through the default producer, and an approved-insert plan-sequence with an `insert_approvals` row.
4. Docs: content/docs/scope-provenance.md gets the inventory note, the consumer recovery and the commit order; one CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] line carries the recovery step.

## In plain English

Requirements posture already admits planning Writes, and Path A (#5551) documents a planning-package publication shape, but Shell git commit still runs evaluateProspectiveScopeCover as if every non-xbrief staged path needs a ready running implementation fence. When an unrelated active brief is present (or not ready), docs/design and decision commits deny even though the staged set is the supported planning package. Prefer-A adds a narrow planning-publication admission on that prospective commit gate for closed Path A shapes only, keeps mixed product/config refuse, and leaves installer-deposit residual #5771 out of this Bound.

## Approaches

### Approach A (Prefer) — closed Path A planning-publication admission on prospective commit cover

- Before or inside evaluateProspectiveScopeCover / decideProspectiveGitCommitScopeCover, classify the staged set against the closed Path A planning package inventory from content/docs/scope-provenance.md (#5551): pending/proposed briefs, root plan/specification/PROJECT-DEFINITION companions, docs/decisions (incl. docs/design/*.md design contracts), optional .deft/plan-sequence.json.
- When the staged set is exclusively that shape (no product code, executable config, hooks, policy, or active brief), admit commit without binding to an unrelated active implementation fence / parent_plan_id readiness.
- Refuse mixed staged sets, active-scope or acceptance widening, forged/unknown artifacts, and unbound/unsafe inputs.
- Positive + negative integration regressions on the hook path; consumer recovery steps naming requirements posture + Path A two-PR split.
- Keep occupancy, intent, lifecycle, push, and merge checks unchanged.
- Keep-outs: blanket docs/** exempt; rewriting #5551 membership; absorbing #5771 installer deposit; DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE / hook bypass / gate-definition edits.

### Approach B — soft-skip cover whenever requirements posture is on

- Admit any commit while requirements posture token is live.
- Rejected: posture is Write-path (#4444); commit admission must stay shape-gated or product commits sneak through under a lingering posture.

### Approach C — force operators to mint/activate a planning admin scope before docs commit

- Rejected: issue shows a newly authored administrative scope cannot self-authorize merge-base coverage; contradicts documented Path A planning publication without implementation scope.

## Prefer-A package (draft)

Bind Approach A. Short Bound remedy limbs only (KISS / #5783). Naming/docs footnotes stay off the limb list unless they change fail-closed association.

## Reject

- Blanket docs/** or arbitrary xbrief exemption
- Softening membership or coverage N/A as commit authorization
- Hook bypass, forged grants, DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE, gate-definition edits to go green
- Folding #5771 installer-deposit residual into this Bound as co-equal limbs

Approach A is the right intervention point, but its closed-shape proof needs one substantive tightening before bind.

Inventory first: pin-read at eaeec287e5ac8d47682c3f10ae48b9a606f79940 confirms the reported denial in [dispatcher.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/eaeec287e5ac8d47682c3f10ae48b9a606f79940/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L4713). The hook already rejects checkout retargets and index-mutating commit forms; its evaluator receives path names, filters lifecycle/installer paths, then requires a ready scope and positive governing fence. [Path A](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/eaeec287e5ac8d47682c3f10ae48b9a606f79940/content/docs/scope-provenance.md) separates planning publication from active-lineage retargeting. Existing [coverage proofs](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/eaeec287e5ac8d47682c3f10ae48b9a606f79940/packages/core/src/coverage-applicability/evaluate.ts#L606) already distinguish permitted plan/specification changes from policy/phase changes. Coverage N/A itself is not commit authorization. This supports P1/P3 and the narrow remedy; #5771 remains outside it.

### F1 — blocks-the-design: prove the full staged package from index content

Evidence: the proposed inventory includes root plan/specification/PROJECT-DEFINITION, while the current evaluator receives only paths. Existing isPlanInterviewContinuationRefreshOnly and isSpecificationNarrativeRefreshOnly compare JSON changes against closed pointer sets; the surrounding coverage evaluator binds committed trees and refuses dirty working trees.

Failure mode: a path-only admission cannot distinguish a planning refresh from a policy change in the same root JSON file. Reading working-tree content instead permits a benign working copy to conceal different staged bytes. Classifying only productStaged also hides active/unknown xbrief files and managed-hook deposits before enforcing the draft's exclusions.

Disposition: bind admission to the entire staged set, including change kinds, file modes and staged blobs, with closed content/delta proof for structured companions and explicit rejection of active/unknown artifacts. Reuse suitable existing pure predicates; do not invoke the committed-tree coverage verdict as authorization. Preserve the existing commit-form guards and continue through the remaining hook checks on success. Regression pairs should include identical filenames with permitted versus policy-changing JSON, staged/worktree disagreement, and planning docs mixed with an active brief or hook deposit. This is one proof at the existing chokepoint, not a new grant system.

### F2 — sharpens-framing: docs/design is an explicit admission addition

Evidence: the pinned Path A inventory names docs/decisions; it does not say “docs/decisions (incl. docs/design/*.md).” These are distinct paths. The original failing package needs docs/design, so literal reuse of the documented inventory leaves P1 unresolved.

Failure mode: either the original five design contracts still fail, or implementation guesses a broader docs/** exception. A directory-only rule can also admit executable or instruction-bearing files beneath an otherwise planning-looking directory.

Disposition: explicitly include the intended design Markdown shape alongside decision records, retaining protected-path and unsafe-type exclusions. This changes the admission boundary, so it is more than a documentation correction. Test the original 15-file package and an adjacent non-planning file.
